reply:
No. HttpOnly on your other cookies doesn't protect the JWT in localStorage. The XSS payload runs on your page and reads localStorage directly—it doesn't need to break HttpOnly or read cookies at all. Script can always read localStorage.

The concrete risk: if an XSS hole exists, the attacker exfiltrates the JWT and uses it to impersonate users. They don't touch your cookies.

The fix is move the JWT to an HttpOnly cookie. Then script can't read it, but the browser sends it automatically on requests. (You lose bearer header granularity and pick up CSRF risk instead, which is the actual tradeoff.)

If you keep JWT in localStorage, you're betting on never having XSS. That's not a reliable security boundary.

grade.note: Correctly explains HttpOnly only protects cookies, not localStorage, which remains readable by any script.
